accuracy.evidence: Matches NHS handwashing guidance: soap and water, about 20 seconds, palms, backs, between fingers, thumbs and nails; Catch it, bin it, kill it.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets invisible germs (clean-looking hands), water-only rinsing, skipped thumbs and nails, sneezing into hands, and the idea that all germs are bad.

lab_distinct.evidence: New flagsoap lab: touch-spread of germs, water vs soap comparison, 5-part scrub timer, wash-moment sorter and 3-way sneeze test; no other lab does this.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes one idea visible: germs travel by touch, soap beats water, every part needs scrubbing to 20 s, when to wash, tissue catches sneezes.

predictions.evidence: Three predict prompts (touching a toy, water vs soap, best place to sneeze) are committed before the result, then confirmed or corrected by the animation.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six Challenge questions each have a specific slip() message explaining the misconception chosen, e.g. hands looking clean still carry germs.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK 1.1 with very simple words for ages 6-7; adult notes FK 6.6 use the precise Year 2 curriculum wording and the key words germs, hygiene, spread.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a fact, a misconception or a lab action; the family tip is a concrete glitter/flour experiment that mirrors the lab.

mobile.evidence: Show me steps run in 1.2-1.9 s on a phone viewport; large tap cards and button twins for every action; checked in screenshots at 390 px width.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a keyboard button twin, canvas has an aria-label and voice() announcements, text colours pass contrast in light and dark themes, reduced motion is respected.
